categories.label: Auth and session
categories.description: Identity, MFA, stale-cookie recovery, and session issuance failures.
symptoms: Users cannot complete login, MFA, recovery, or refresh.
Audit shows repeated auth/session failures for the same workspace or actor.
firstChecks: Review failed auth audit events filtered by result and action.
Confirm MFA policy, session lifecycle, and proxy/BFF auth recovery are healthy.
Check whether the issue is isolated to one workspace, provider, browser, or region.
remediation: Keep session validation fail-closed while restoring the failing auth dependency.
Use support-read context only when the workspace owner explicitly needs investigation support.
Escalate to Security / Identity before changing MFA or session policy defaults.
evidence: Failed auth audit events with request IDs and actor context.
Session lifecycle guard output and proxy/BFF auth recovery traces.
User-reported browser, workspace, and timestamp.
categories.userMessageGuidance: Acknowledge sign-in or verification trouble without exposing policy internals, secrets, provider errors, or session identifiers.

categories.label: Gateway runtime
categories.description: Gateway-daemon heartbeat, WireGuard readiness, endpoint reachability, and host runtime issues.
symptoms: Gateway health is down or degraded.
WireGuard config readiness cannot find an eligible healthy gateway.
firstChecks: Open Gateways and inspect heartbeat, endpoint, observed port, and runtime reasons.
Confirm gateway-daemon has host networking, NET_ADMIN, and WireGuard interface visibility.
Check gateway-manager desired-state delivery and last apply result.
remediation: Restore gateway-daemon host prerequisites and connectivity.
Reconcile configured vs observed WireGuard port before retrying runtime apply.
Keep customer-facing status scoped to affected gateway or region.
evidence: Gateway ID, region, endpoint posture, and lastSeen timestamp.
Gateway-daemon logs and observed runtime state.
Rejected gateway reasons from status incident details.
categories.userMessageGuidance: State that a gateway path is degraded or unavailable; do not expose host commands, internal topology, or unrelated tenant details.

categories.label: Route and path apply
categories.description: Route policy validation, route apply mode, path ownership, and route runtime apply failures.
symptoms: Route changes do not affect traffic.
Gateway-daemon rejects routing desired state or reports overlapping CIDRs.
firstChecks: Confirm ROUTING_APPLY_MODE and whether routes are expected to be live.
Inspect route ownership, destination CIDRs, and gateway assignment.
Review route mutation audit metadata for owner, actor, and scope.
remediation: Fix invalid CIDRs or target assignment, then save and retry reconcile.
Move ROUTING_APPLY_MODE to apply only when route enforcement is intended.
Escalate ownership disputes to the route policy owner before forcing changes.
evidence: Route ID, owner posture, apply mode, and failed gateway apply details.
Audit event for the most recent route mutation.
Gateway-daemon route apply log snippet with secrets removed.
categories.userMessageGuidance: Describe route policy as pending, disabled, or rejected; avoid claiming live traffic changes until runtime apply confirms them.

categories.label: DNS resolution
categories.description: DNS policy validation, propagation, group disablement, and runtime DNS apply failures.
symptoms: Managed names fail to resolve or DNS changes remain pending.
Gateway-daemon rejects DNS runtime state.
firstChecks: Open DNS Zones, Nameservers, and Settings to verify desired records and disablement groups.
Check propagation status and gateway-daemon DNS apply logs.
Confirm whether the affected device or group is intentionally excluded.
remediation: Correct invalid zone, nameserver, or match rules before retrying runtime refresh.
Remove disabled-management groups only when DNS should be managed for that scope.
Keep DNS and route remediation separate unless both incidents share the same gateway failure.
evidence: Affected DNS zone, nameserver, group, and gateway scope.
DNS runtime apply status and sanitized error summary.
Recent DNS policy audit events.
categories.userMessageGuidance: Explain which DNS scope is affected and whether management is disabled or failing; do not expose internal resolver topology.

categories.label: Access and ownership
categories.description: RBAC, group access, route ownership, support-read, and privileged investigation boundaries.
symptoms: Users cannot access an expected workspace, route, or operation.
Support or break-glass access is denied or requires review.
firstChecks: Review backend effective-access explanation before trusting frontend state.
Check group membership, role assignment, support-read grant, and route owner posture.
Inspect audit events for denied permission, delegated actor, or break-glass context.
remediation: Change access through guarded workspace/admin flows only.
Do not accept browser-supplied actor, owner, tenant, or delegated authority.
Escalate suspicious permission drift to Security before granting broad access.
evidence: Effective access response, audit event ID, actor, workspace, and requested action.
Group and role assignment snapshot at the time of denial.
Support-read or break-glass approval context.
categories.userMessageGuidance: Keep customer messaging focused on access review or missing permission; do not disclose internal role names beyond the product role shown to the user.

categories.label: Audit and log sink
categories.description: Durable audit retention, audit export posture, and external log-sink delivery failures.
symptoms: External Elasticsearch/OpenSearch audit export is failing.
Audit failure spikes appear in operator status.
firstChecks: Confirm Platform Audit still shows durable Nanami audit events.
Open Company Settings and inspect log-sink delivery status, credential reference, and endpoint.
Check whether delivery errors are retryable and when the last attempt happened.
remediation: Restore endpoint reachability, index permissions, or credential reference.
Retry external export only after confirming durable audit events remain intact.
Do not rotate or print raw sink credentials during incident response.
evidence: Delivery status, retryable flag, last attempt timestamp, and redacted error summary.
Platform Audit query showing durable event availability.
Operator change audit for log-sink settings.
categories.userMessageGuidance: State that external audit export is delayed while durable audit records remain stored in Nanami.

categories.label: Connector and integration
categories.description: Connector lifecycle metadata, first-wave availability, and unsupported connector posture.
symptoms: Operator expects a connector that is not in the shipped first wave.
Connector lifecycle or integration status is unclear.
firstChecks: Check connector lifecycle metadata and managed-in surface.
Confirm the connector is part of current release scope before promising availability.
Review settings mutation audit for rejected or unsupported connector changes.
remediation: Keep unsupported connectors as roadmap, not partially enabled runtime claims.
Update operator-facing copy only when a connector has a real lifecycle and management surface.
Escalate scope changes to Product Integrations.
evidence: Connector ID, lifecycle state, managed-in surface, and settings audit event.
First-wave connector contract output.
Operator request or integration support ticket.
categories.userMessageGuidance: Use availability language only for shipped connectors; do not imply unsupported connectors are configured or live.

categories.label: Control-plane availability
categories.description: Control-plane status source failures, backend unavailable snapshots, and platform/system status source gaps.
symptoms: Status cannot load live control-plane or aggregate sources.
Dashboard uses a stale snapshot or cannot determine source health.
firstChecks: Check control-plane health, database reachability, and BFF upstream configuration.
Identify which source failed before declaring the whole platform unavailable.
Confirm whether a stale snapshot is being shown and when it was generated.
remediation: Restore control-plane or source dependency reachability.
Keep unavailable sources visible instead of flattening them into healthy status.
Use the degraded/unavailable source message as the public-safe status basis.
evidence: Failed source name, normalized error, request ID, and generatedAt timestamp.
Control-plane logs and database health checks.
Dashboard BFF upstream configuration snapshot.
categories.userMessageGuidance: Say that status data is currently unavailable or stale; do not claim no incidents when sources failed.

categories.label: Deployment, config, and secrets
categories.description: Deploy preflight, runtime secret validation, internal mTLS, and key material misconfiguration.
symptoms: Deploy or startup fails due to missing, placeholder, weak, or malformed key material.
Internal mTLS or runtime secret validation blocks service startup.
firstChecks: Run the relevant deploy/config preflight and runtime secret boundary guard.
Confirm operator-managed env files contain real secrets and tracked examples contain placeholders only.
Check internal mTLS certificate validity and service identity expectations.
remediation: Generate or rotate the missing operator-managed secret without printing it in logs.
Preserve existing non-placeholder keys unless an explicit rotation plan exists.
Restart affected services only after config validation passes.
evidence: Preflight failure line, affected env key name, and service name.
Runtime secret boundary guard output.
Change record for key generation or rotation.
categories.userMessageGuidance: Avoid exposing secret values; mention only the affected configuration class and remediation owner.

categories.label: Public distribution and install
categories.description: Community public distribution, install channel availability, docs truth, and release gate posture.
symptoms: Community public install path is referenced before anonymous distribution is actually available.
Docs, deploy, or release checks disagree about current public availability.
firstChecks: Confirm the real anonymous public GitHub/GHCR or release-bundle channel state.
Run the Community distribution contract and public content boundary checks.
Check whether Product explicitly deferred public distribution from release scope.
remediation: Keep docs aligned with actual availability until the public channel is real.
Do not close the distribution blocker unless anonymous install/pull works or Product defers it.
Update release notes and operator guidance only after the channel decision is final.
evidence: Public channel test result and failing/passing command output.
Docs/public content boundary output.
Product decision record for release inclusion or deferral.
categories.userMessageGuidance: Be explicit about availability: do not imply public install works until the channel is truly open.
